perspective:
I, Bradley Ochoa, have access to the following:

- I am a salesperson at a marketing firm. Katherine Lasiloo is my colleague and the marketing manager. Our professional relationship is generally cordial but sometimes strained by disagreements over sales and marketing strategy.
- In a meeting room, I brought data and charts from our last five campaigns to argue that traditional sales methods deserve more consideration. I told Katherine I appreciated her digital strategies but believed core sales could benefit more from traditional methods.
- I heard Katherine say she saw my point, but the market is evolving, digital outreach has potential, and she asked how I reconcile my data with increasing online engagement rates.
- I told her I was not suggesting abandoning digital marketing, but I was frustrated that proven traditional methods felt sidelined without proper consideration. She said it was about balance and suggested analyzing the data together to integrate both approaches.
- After that meeting, Katherine shared recent digital campaign success stories that significantly boosted engagement and sales. I found the results impressive and asked how those strategies were developed.
- Katherine told me it was about targeting the right audience with the right message, and she offered to walk me through the analytics and decision-making behind a recent campaign. I admitted my doubts about moving away from traditional methods and said the outcomes made me want to understand digital better. She said she was glad I was open and suggested diving deeper into the data.
- I proposed a joint strategy meeting to combine traditional and digital approaches. Katherine agreed, saying combining our strengths could lead to better results and suggesting we schedule time to brainstorm and outline next steps.
- After our joint meeting, I was excited and worked overtime on a board presentation integrating both our ideas. I told Katherine about the draft. She reviewed it, called it comprehensive and well thought out, and praised my hard work. I thanked her, said I was convinced the integrated approach would set us apart from competitors, and said I wanted to nail the presentation. She was confident and suggested fine-tuning it together.
- After the presentation succeeded and the new strategy was implemented, I felt grateful for my professional growth and our collaboration. I thanked Katherine and said I had learned a lot. She said my openness to new ideas made it a successful partnership. I proposed regular strategy sessions, and she agreed.
- I only have access to what Katherine said, what she showed or shared with me, and what I observed her do. I do not have access to her private thoughts, personality, background, or unspoken motivations.
